bug_semantics: A remote unauthenticated ForwardOpen can supply a mixed-class CIP application path (Assembly as path1 plus a non-Assembly endpoint such as Identity instance 1 or Ethernet Link). check_path()/ResolveInstances() accept any existing class+instance and bind those objects as consuming/producing I/O endpoints; class 0/1 handling does not require kCipAssemblyClass. CipConnMgrClass::forward_open then dispatches via mgmnt_class (path1 Assembly) into CipAssemblyClass::OpenConnection -> OpenIO -> ConnectionData::CorrectSizes, which forces attribute 3 and casts instance data to ByteBuf*/CipByteArray. Identity attribute 3 is uint16_t product_code_ and Ethernet Link attribute 3 is a 6-byte MAC, so ByteBuf::size() (limit-start) reads off the true object (ASan global-buffer-overflow on product_code_, heap-buffer-overflow on physical_address) and aborts the POSIX sample server.
flaw_origin: On 2016-10-15, 2d6b8f3eaafde2e6090cf76966b3d338f7e2b4f6 first wrote check_path() to resolve each ForwardOpen app path by that path's own class+instance and stored those CipInstance* as consuming/producing endpoints, while the I/O size-correction path stopped re-looking-up endpoints through GetCipClass(kCipAssemblyClassCode)->Instance() and instead treated the already-bound instance's attribute 3 as a byte array. Immediate parent 0442159a0a1369b0ae7722dc42b2b70c03d3c41e still parsed later paths as instance/connpt IDs on path1's class and opened I/O only via assembly_class->Instance(), so mixed-class Identity/Ethernet endpoints could not reach the CipByteArray cast. Later 90721b00/aec5f674/08d3a45 only moved/renamed this logic (check_path into cipconnection.cc, ResolveInstances extraction, class 0/1 SetServer(false) without an Assembly check). Fix ea870a274bf68dfaa3f511f20e2fff6778fb7b74 restores the Assembly-class invariant for class 0/1 config/consuming/producing paths.

The issue #45 PoC and ASan stack make the mechanism concrete: mixed-class ForwardOpen is accepted, then CorrectSizes type-confuses a non-Assembly attribute 3 (product_code_ / physical_address) as a ByteBuf and OOB-reads. The security fix is ea870a2, which inserts the missing Assembly-class checks in ResolveInstances for class 0/1 rather than hardening CorrectSizes. The smallest first-write of that reachable flaw is 2d6b8f3e (2016-10-15): it introduced per-path check_path() binding of arbitrary CIP instances as I/O endpoints and simultaneously stopped using assembly_class->Instance() in the size-correction path. Parent 0442159a is present and still Assembly-only on both the path parser and I/O open, so the mixed-class attack is absent there. 2d6b8f3e is a regular single-parent commit, not a squash/merge that can be decomposed; later C++ moves/renames are not BICs.
